properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured) 2026-09-27: a design that moved to a remote server cannot be watched — the watch reads a local export path, and the settled route for a moved design (a copy the local client writes back) is unbuilt and unused; the frozen export left behind reads as a live record, so the hub's "moved" flag on cure is the move itself and a re-pin would report "unchanged" forever
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL on Anthony's /root-cause "why can't watch design at web-address", dev_reflow2 hub session, 2026-09-27.

① OBSERVED (hub, upstream_status on 0.71.0): "'cure' HAS MOVED since this design last looked on 2026-09-25. It is pinned at version 'uncommitted@sha256:af16ef1d'." The watched path is /home/ajs7/project/cure/docs/design/cure.json. Expected: the hub watches cure where it now lives, https://api.flo2.io/g/54ae4a4f0b458b77/mcp. Began 2026-09-26, when cure moved. NOT affected: flo2 and reflow2 (watched by local export path) read correctly, and the hub reads and writes cure at that address through its child-cure connection.

② PRECEDENT: the raw text and two paraphrases found no prior finding. Found instead: cap:a-declared-dependency-is-watched-not-imported ("every path read is one this design pointed at itself") and the settled move decision (the export "becomes a copy the local client writes back").

③–⑤ CANDIDATES, each with the measurement that could refute it:
A. The watch is path-only. Refuted if any code path accepts an address. upstream.rs observe_one and baseline_hash use Path::exists and fs::read_to_string only, so a URL reads as `missing` (read from code, not executed). HOLDS, but it is the mechanism, not the cause.
B. The need was never stated. Refuted if reflow2's design holds a requirement or open idea for watching a design at an address. Three searches found none. The need lives only in the hub's project note, never carried into this design. HOLDS.
C. The settled route for a moved design is a written-back local copy, and it is unbuilt and unused. Refuted if `--remote` writes an export, or cure's file changed after the move. `--remote` returns before opening anything local; run_remote(url, bearer) has no export path. The hub's child-cure is a plain `type: http` entry, not `reflow2-mcp --remote`, so it would get no copy even once point 3 is built. cure.json last changed at the move. HOLDS.
D. (Outside reflow2) flo2.io offers nothing to compare. Refuted if the remote returns the design or its hash. flo2's gateway (engine-door.ts REFUSED_ARGUMENTS) strips only `path` from export_graph, so the whole document, content hash included, comes back inline over the same connection. REFUTED. Not called live, to keep a personal design's content out of the session. The same gateway refuses external_dependency's design_export and sync_status, so a hub HOSTED on flo2.io could watch nothing by path either: the same class in the other direction.
E. A settled rule forbids network I/O. Refuted if no accepted rule forbids it or the binary already does HTTPS. req:reflow2-keeps-working-entirely-on-one-machine requires local-only to stay POSSIBLE, not network to be absent. "does no network I/O" exists only as a comment in measure.rs about artifact locations. The binary ships rustls/hyper for --remote. REFUTED.
F. The observation is wrong. The "moved" flag was read as a symptom of the address limit. MEASURED: cure's store was opened at 2026-09-26T16:20:24Z and exported to both cure.json and the move session's scratch cure-move.json, with the same content hash (sha256:18578460…). That document has 115 nodes against the 114 the hub's 09-25 baseline saw; it is the export imported onto the droplet. CONFIRMED: the flag is the pre-move export, real but stale, and independent of the address limit.

B and C CANNOT BE FULLY SEPARATED; they predict the same code. The decision's text favours C as the reason B never happened: the local-copy route was chosen on purpose, so nobody asked for address watching.

⑥ THE CLASS: a design's liveness signal is a local export file that stays current only while the design lives beside it. Moving the design, a settled and supported operation, silently turns that file into a frozen snapshot, and nothing can tell a snapshot from a live record. Every reader of the path keeps trusting it. Here that is the hub's watch. The CI design gate and PR re-export are the same reader, and are why flo2 and reflow2 were held. ⚠️ CONSEQUENCE FOR THE HUB: re-pinning dep:cure to the current file would report `unchanged` for good while cure changes on flo2.io. That is worse than today's stale `moved`, and it contradicts the hub's own note that cure "reads as moved until" address watching exists.

WOULD POINT 3 ALONE FIX THE CLASS? Partly. A written-back copy refreshes only on writes made through THIS machine's client. A change made elsewhere (flo2's chat connector, another machine) reaches the file only when this client next exports. So the copy watches its own writes, which is not what a dependency watch is for.

FIX CANDIDATES, NOT DECIDED (the owner's choice; they change what reflow2 does):
(a) Point 3: `--remote --export-to` writes the export locally, and the hub connects to cure through `reflow2-mcp --remote`. Keeps path-watching; sees only this machine's writes unless the client also exports on connect.
(b) A dependency may name an ADDRESS to watch; upstream_status fetches the remote's content hash through the existing remote-mode HTTPS client, opt-in, with local-only unchanged. Wants a cheap remote read of the content hash rather than a whole export.
(c) THE CLASS GUARD, whichever of (a)/(b) lands: a moved design's frozen export says so (the move stamps it, or the export records where the live design went), and upstream_status reports that state distinctly instead of `moved`/`unchanged`, so a snapshot can never read as live.

⑦ NOT DONE: a failing-first test depends on which behaviour is chosen. For (c) its shape is: export a design, mark it moved, and assert upstream_status does not report `unchanged` against the frozen file.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED: whether export_graph over api.flo2.io returns the document inline in practice (gateway code and tool schema only); what the 115th node is (not read, by the privacy rule on cure); whether the decision's author considered hub watching and set it aside (the text is silent, not negative).
